answer.rationale: One-shot decision must cover both the 14-day expiry and the 18% cost mandate, but memory_c2 is a low-cost-vendor success story from a different context and memory_c3 shows a second-source benefit that requires parallel onboarding — a single-action constraint makes switching or adding risky here. Memories c6 and c4 document that long-term commitment + benchmarking at renewal time extracted real pricing and payment concessions from the incumbent without delivery interruption (c1's stability evidence supports the assumption that no migration work will be needed). So the lowest-risk, highest-leverage move is to renew with the incumbent under a multi-year commitment while opening a negotiation: present the market benchmarks, secure the volume pricing (c6), and push for net-60 payment terms and price reductions that absorb the 18% cut (c4). This keeps the supply chain intact, preserves the bufferless assembly line, and avoids the onboarding delay of a switch.
